text:
leah: Heads up — monitoring alerted for a rack (rack-12) with increased PCIe AER counts + NVLink transient link flutters. Seen perf regressions on multi-GPU jobs, tail latency up ~3x.

matt: saw the alert, which nodes specifically?

leah: nodes g12-{03..06} (4 hosts). alert group shows repeated `AER: corrected error` then `nvlink: link down` in kernel logs. dmesg snippet I pulled: 
```
[ 1234.567890] pcieport 0000:04:00.0: AER: multiple Uncorrected (NonFatal) error detected
[ 1234.567920] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:81:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1234.567930] nvlink0: link 1 flapped, state DOWN -> UP
```

jin: ugh. Xid 79 usually bus resets. Are these all on same PCI root?

leah: yes, all attached to the same IO-aggregator (pci root 0000:81). lspci shows same bridge.

sara: any ECC errors?

leah: ECC corrected count rising but not massive. Mostly Xid and NVLink flaps.

ryan: initial mitigation — we should drain affected nodes and switch workloads off before they get forced OOM/fail. I can start cordon+drain for g12-03..06.

matt: +1. also add to routing policy to avoid selecting those SKUs for low-latency models until we confirm hardware health.

deploy-bot: auto-scaling triggered: +6 GPUs in us-west-2 to handle shifted load.

jin: for triage: capture full dmesg, nvidia-smi -q, lspci -vvv, and nvlink status. Also enable persistent logging for the nodes. I’ll open a vendor ticket.

leah: pasted nvidia-smi -q for g12-04: 
```
GPU 0: Tesla-A100
    Xid Errors: 79 (last seen 2025-11-03 15:12:34)
    ECC : Corrected: 1024, Uncorrected: 0
NVLink: link0: 4 lanes, avg error rate spike 0.8%
```

ryan: good capture. jin — include nvlink bridge fw and GPU BIOS versions. Past issues were resolved by updating NVLink bridge firmware on our custom interposer.

jin: noted. vendor asked for tcg logs and `setpci -s` outputs. I’ll request RMA for the suspect cards if fw update doesn't help.

matt: question — do we want to temporarily disable AER to reduce noisy resets while we test? (pci=noaer)

leah: we discussed pci=noaer before — it hides symptoms but can mask real hardware problems. prefer: keep AER, enable more detailed recovery logging, and avoid pci=noaer unless vendor recommends.

ryan: agree. also check BIOS versions for the host bridge and enable PCIe relaxed ordering fixes if available.

jin: trying a non-invasive test on one host: pulled one GPU and reinserted the NVLink bridge, then ran 30m stress. If flaps stop -> bad bridge or seating. If not -> DB/host root or switch.

leah: meanwhile I’ll flip traffic: add a temporary routing rule in the serving mesh to route latency-sensitive traffic to other racks/region fallback. Patch pushed to routing: 
```json
{"policy":"avoid: rack-12","duration":"2h","reason":"nvlink/pci errors"}
```

matt: good. Sara can you update on SLO impact and cost delta?

sara: estimated increased infra spend ~+12% for the next 24h due to ASG spinup + cross-region egress. SLA risk low because of fallback; tail latencies might be higher for a subset of requests.

jin: update: performed firmware diff — GPU fw is one version behind recommended but vendor says that alone unlikely to fix NVLink flaps. They want NVLink bridge fw and host BIOS. Opening case RN. Case ID: VEND-8421.

ryan: action list so far: 
- cordon+drain g12-03..06 (in progress)
- capture and attach logs to VEND-8421 (jin)
- test reseating NVLink bridge on g12-04 (jin)
- schedule maintenance out-of-band for NVLink bridge fw + BIOS if vendor approves (leah)
- tag affected GPUs for RMA if flaps persist (jin)

leah: I also updated runbook pointer: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/pci-nvlink-triage — add your findings there.

matt: a quick note on detection: we should add a derived metric that correlates NVLink flaps + Xid 79 rate per host and alert when >5 events / 10m. Current alert only looks at AER count.

sara: agree. that will help catch early degradations and avoid large-scale spillovers. I’ll file a ticket to update monitoring.

jin: one more observation — the flaps coincide with a nightly backup job that saturates PCIe bandwidth on that aggregation path. I’m going to throttle that job for the rack as an experiment.

leah: nice catch. throttle applied.

deploy-bot: autoscaler: added 6 GPUs in us-west-2 (type a100-80gb) at 15:23 UTC.

ryan: status update 15:30 UTC — drains complete, instance g12-03..06 in maintenance. No further flaps observed on g12-04 after reseat test (30m). Still collecting full 4-hour logs before closing.

matt: if reseat fixed it, could be mechanical seating or interposer. Still do vendor case and plan RMA for the bridge assembly if vendor requests.

jin: vendor replied — wants us to run `nvidia-persistenced` in debug mode and gather nvlink error counters over 24h. They flagged possible thermal expansion causing marginal contact.

leah: ok we'll keep nodes drained for the maintenance window and schedule a cold reboot + bridge reseat in next 48h. Communicate to workloads to prefer Dedicated capacity or other regions for the window.

sara: I’ll update the outage/maintenance calendar and product owners. Estimated user-visible impact: low but internal model jobs may see queueing. Cost estimate for RMA + extra capacity ~ $7k one-time + $2k/day while held.

matt: long term items: 1) add nvlink/pcie health scoreboard into cluster capacity planner, 2) consider spare NVLink bridges in each datacenter, 3) update pre-boarding host firmware checklist.

leah: agreed. I’ll draft a post-mortem after we have full logs. For now, keeping this thread for live updates—please add any logs to the vendor ticket and the runbook. :thumbsup:
